title: The Lost Puppy
description: Read the story, then answer the questions in your own words.
story:
One afternoon, Sara was walking home from school when she heard a small barking sound behind a tree. She looked and saw a tiny puppy shivering in the cold. The puppy had no collar and looked very hungry.

Sara gently picked up the puppy and took it home. She gave it some food and water. Later that evening, Sara and her father made posters to help find the puppy's owner.

The next day, a neighbor saw the poster and came to Sara's house. The puppy happily ran to the neighbor because it belonged to him. The neighbor thanked Sara for taking care of his puppy.

Sara felt happy because she helped someone in need.

Name TWO things Sara did to help the puppy.

title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
description: Read the fable, then answer the questions below.
story:
All summer long, the ant worked hard. Every day she carried food to her nest underground. The grasshopper watched and laughed. Why do you work so hard? he sang. Come play with me instead! The ant shook her head. Winter is coming. I must prepare.

When winter arrived, the grasshopper was cold and hungry. He had nothing stored away. He knocked on the ant's door and begged for food. The ant shared a little, but said kindly, Next summer, remember to work while the sun shines.

The grasshopper nodded and promised he would never forget that lesson again.

acceptableAnswers: shared food and told him to prepare next time

title: Place Value, Standard Form, Expanded Form & Rounding
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions. Take your time!
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. PLACE VALUE: The value of where a digit sits in a number.
   In 495: 4=Hundreds(400), 9=Tens(90), 5=Ones(5)

2. STANDARD FORM: Writing a number using digits.
   two thousand forty = 2,040

3. EXPANDED FORM: Break the number apart to show each digit's value.
   356 = 300 + 50 + 6
   495 = 400 + 90 + 5

4. ROUNDING: Make a number simpler by rounding to the nearest ten or hundred.
   RULE: Look at the digit to the RIGHT of where you round.
   5 or more = round UP. 4 or less = round DOWN.
   79 rounds UP to 80. 34 rounds DOWN to 30. 462 rounds to 500.

title: Estimation, Unknown Numbers & Inverse Operations
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. FRONT-END ESTIMATION: Keep only the highest place value digit, make the rest zeros.
   458 becomes 400. 678 becomes 700. 311 becomes 300.

2. UNKNOWN NUMBER: A missing number shown as ? or a letter.
   24 + ? = 83. Think: 83 - 24 = 59, so ? = 59
   A - 42 = 200. Think: 200 + 42 = 242, so A = 242

3. INVERSE OPERATIONS: The OPPOSITE operation that UNDOES another.
   Addition undoes Subtraction. Multiplication undoes Division.

4. DECOMPOSE (Expanded Subtraction):
   678 - 548 = ? Break apart first!
   600+70+8 minus 500+40+8 = 100+30+0 = 130

title: Multiplication: Arrays, Repeated Addition & Doubles
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. MULTIPLICATION: Adding the same number over and over, but faster!
   3 x 4 = 12 means 3 groups of 4.

2. REPEATED ADDITION: 3 x 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12

3. ARRAY: Objects in ROWS (left to right) and COLUMNS (up and down).
   A 3x4 array = 3 rows, 4 columns = 12 total

4. DOUBLES: Multiplying by 2, or adding a number to itself.
   8 + 8 = 16 AND 8 x 2 = 16

title: Multiplication Properties
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. COMMUTATIVE PROPERTY: Order does NOT matter.
   3 x 4 = 12 AND 4 x 3 = 12 (same answer!)

2. ZERO PROPERTY: Any number x 0 = 0.
   5 x 0 = 0. 999 x 0 = 0.

3. IDENTITY PROPERTY: Any number x 1 = that number.
   225 x 1 = 225. 7 x 1 = 7.

4. DISTRIBUTIVE PROPERTY: Break one factor into a sum of two numbers.
   6 x 4 = (3 x 4) + (3 x 4) = 12 + 12 = 24

title: Division: Groups, Fact Families & Repeated Subtraction
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. DIVISION: Separating a whole amount into EQUAL parts.
   20 divided by 4 = 5 (20 split into 4 groups = 5 in each)

2. DIVIDEND / DIVISOR / QUOTIENT:
   20 / 4 = 5
   20 = DIVIDEND (number being split)
   4 = DIVISOR (number of groups)
   5 = QUOTIENT (number in each group)

3. FACT FAMILY: All related x and / facts for the same 3 numbers.
   2 x 4 = 8 | 4 x 2 = 8 | 8 / 4 = 2 | 8 / 2 = 4

4. REPEATED SUBTRACTION: Subtract the same number over and over until you reach 0.
   12 / 3: 12-3=9, 9-3=6, 6-3=3, 3-3=0. You subtracted 4 times, so answer = 4.

title: 2D Shapes: Triangles, Quadrilaterals, Angles & Vertices
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. TRIANGLES: A 2-D closed shape with exactly 3 sides and 3 angles.
   Equilateral Triangle = ALL 3 sides equal in length.

2. QUADRILATERAL: Any polygon with FOUR sides.
   Types: Square, Rectangle, Rhombus, Parallelogram, Trapezoid, Kite

3. ANGLE & RIGHT ANGLE:
   Angle = formed when two line segments meet at a vertex.
   Right Angle = exactly 90 degrees (looks like a square corner).

4. VERTEX (plural VERTICES):
   The corner/endpoint where two or more line segments meet.
   Triangle = 3 vertices. Square = 4 vertices.

title: Special Quadrilaterals, Polygons & Parallel Lines
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. SPECIAL QUADRILATERALS:
   Parallelogram = 2 pairs of parallel sides
   Rhombus = parallelogram with 4 EQUAL sides
   Square = 4 equal sides AND 4 right angles
   Rectangle = 4 right angles
   Trapezoid = only 1 pair of parallel sides
   Kite = 2 pairs of adjacent equal sides

2. REGULAR vs IRREGULAR POLYGON:
   Regular = ALL equal sides AND all equal angles (e.g. equilateral triangle, square)
   Irregular = sides or angles are NOT all equal

3. CLASSIFY: Sort shapes into groups based on shared attributes.

4. PARALLEL LINES: Lines that always stay the same distance apart and NEVER cross.
   Like train tracks!

title: Fractions: Numerator, Denominator & Equivalents
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. FRACTION: An amount broken into equal size pieces.
   Written as numerator / denominator. Example: 1/2 (one-half)

2. NUMERATOR: The TOP number. Tells HOW MANY parts we have.
   In 3/6, the numerator is 3.

3. DENOMINATOR: The BOTTOM number. Tells TOTAL equal parts in the whole.
   In 3/6, the denominator is 6.

4. EQUIVALENT FRACTIONS: Different fractions that are equal in value.
   1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8 (all equivalent!)
   Use > (greater than) or < (less than) to compare.

title: Measurement: Length & Time
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. LENGTH UNITS:
   Inches (in) = 12 inches = 1 foot
   Quarter inch = 1/4 of an inch
   Half inch = 1/2 of an inch
   Feet (ft) = 12 inches
   Yards (yd) = 3 feet (a football field is 100 yards!)

2. PERIMETER: The distance AROUND a shape. Add all sides.
   Rectangle 15cm x 5cm: 15+5+15+5 = 40 cm

3. TIME:
   Minute = 60 seconds
   Hour = 60 minutes
   1 day = 24 hours

4. ELAPSED TIME: How much time has passed.
   Start 3:30 PM, End 4:05 PM = 35 minutes elapsed.

title: Area, Perimeter & Square Units
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. SQUARE UNIT: A square with an area of 1. Used to measure area.
   Written as cm2, in2, ft2, etc.

2. AREA: The SPACE INSIDE a shape.
   Area of Rectangle = Length x Width
   8 cm x 3 cm = 24 cm2

3. PERIMETER (Review): Distance AROUND the outside.
   P = L+W+L+W or P = 2L+2W
   8 cm x 3 cm rectangle: P = 8+3+8+3 = 22 cm

4. AREA MODEL: A rectangle drawn to show multiplication.
   Used for distributive property too!
   6 x 4 area model can be split as (3x4)+(3x4)=24

title: Data & Graphs
description: Read the key vocabulary below, then answer the questions.
story:
TODAY'S 4 TOPICS

1. TALLY MARKS & FREQUENCY TABLE:
   Tally mark = way to count (4 lines + 1 crossing = 5)
   Frequency table = organizes data and shows how many times something occurred.

2. BAR GRAPH: Represents data with vertical or horizontal bars.
   X Axis = the BOTTOM horizontal line of the graph
   Y Axis = the SIDE vertical line of the graph

3. PICTURE GRAPH: Uses pictures/symbols to show data.
   Each picture has a KEY showing how many it represents.
   Example: smiley face = 2 votes

4. READING DATA:
   HOW MANY MORE = subtract the two values
   HOW MANY TOTAL = add all values
   Example: Dogs=10, Cats=8, Snakes=5, Rabbits=2 Total = 10+8+5+2 = 25

title: Surah An-Naba — Complete (All 40 Ayat)
description: Read ALL 40 ayat with your parent. Read Arabic, then transliteration, then meaning. Then answer the questions!
story:
SURAH AN-NABA (The Great News) Surah 78 — All 40 Ayat

── PART 1: THE QUESTION (Ayat 1-5) ──
1. Amma yatasaa-aloon — About what are they asking one another?
2. Anil naba-il azeem — About the great news
3. Allathee hum feehi mukhtalifoon — That over which they disagree
4. Kalla saya-lamoon — No! They are going to know.
5. Thumma kalla saya-lamoon — Then, no! They are going to know.

── PART 2: ALLAH'S SIGNS (Ayat 6-16) ──
6. Alam naj-alil arda mihadaa — Have We not made the earth a resting place?
7. Wal jibala awtadaa — And the mountains as stakes?
8. Wa khalaqnakum azwajaa — And We created you in pairs.
9. Wa ja-alna nawmakum subataa — And made your sleep a means of rest.
10. Wa ja-alnal layla libasaa — And made the night as clothing.
11. Wa ja-alnan nahara ma-ashaa — And made the day for livelihood.
12. Wa banayna fawqakum sab-an shidadaa — And built above you seven strong heavens.
13. Wa ja-alna sirajan wahajaa — And made a blazing lamp (the sun).
14. Wa anzalna minal mu-sirati ma-an thajjajaa — And sent down from the rain clouds pouring water.
15. Linukhrija bihi habban wa nabataa — That We may bring forth grain and vegetation.
16. Wa jannatin alfafaa — And gardens of entwined growth.

── PART 3: THE DAY OF JUDGMENT (Ayat 17-20) ──
17. Inna yawmal fasli kana meqataa — Indeed, the Day of Judgment is an appointed time.
18. Yawma yunfakhu fis suri fata-toona afwajaa — The Day the Horn is blown and you come in multitudes.
19. Wa futihatil sama-u fakanat abwabaa — And the heaven is opened and becomes gateways.
20. Wa suyyiratil jibalu fakanat sarabaa — And the mountains are removed and become a mirage.

── PART 4: THE PUNISHMENT (Ayat 21-30) ──
21. Inna jahannama kanat mirsadaa — Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait
22. Lil tagheena ma-abaa — For the transgressors, a place of return.
23. Labiteena feeha ahqabaa — In which they will remain for ages unending.
24. La yathooqoona feeha bardan wa la sharabaa — They will taste no coolness therein, nor any drink
25. Illa hameeman wa ghassaqaa — Except scalding water and foul purulence.
26. Jaza-an Wifaqaa — A fitting recompense.
   MEMORIZE AYAH 26: Word 1 = Jaza-an (recompense) + Word 2 = Wifaqaa (fitting)
27. Innahum kaanu la yarjoona hisabaa — Indeed, they were not expecting an account.
28. Wa kaththabu bi-ayatina kiththabaa — And denied Our signs with emphatic denial.
29. Wa kulla shay-in ahsaynahu kitabaa — But all things We have enumerated in writing.
30. Fathooqoo falan nazeedakum illa ataabaa — So taste the penalty, and We will increase only your torment.

── PART 5: REWARD FOR THE RIGHTEOUS (Ayat 31-36) ──
31. Inna lil muttaqeena mafazaa — Indeed, for the righteous is attainment
32. Hada-iqa wa a-naabaa — Gardens and grapevines.
33. Wa kawa-iba atrabaa — And companions of equal age.
34. Wa ka-san dihaqaa — And a full cup.
35. La yasma-oona feeha laghwan wa la kiththabaa — No ill speech or falsehood will they hear therein.
36. Jaza-am mir rabbika ataa-an hisabaa — As a generous reward from your Lord.

── PART 6: THE FINAL TRUTH (Ayat 37-40) ──
37. Rabb is-samawati wal ardi wa ma baynahuma ar-rahmani la yamlikoona minhu khitabaa — Lord of the heavens and earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful. None can speak to Him without permission.
38. Yawma yaqoomur roohu wal mala-ikatu saffan — The Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows — none speak except whom the Most Merciful permits.
39. Thalikal yawmul haqq — That is the True Day; so whoever wills may return to his Lord.
40. Inna antharnakum ataaban qareeban yawma yanthorul mar-o ma qaddamat yadahu wa yaqoolul kafiru ya laytani kuntu turabaa — We warned you of a near punishment. On that Day, a man will see what his hands have done, and the disbeliever will say: Oh, I wish I were dust!
